goal: Find reusable parts, approaches and user-flow evidence for a OneNote-style Windows notes app with an always-on-top quick-note widget.

questions.question: Which maintained open-source rich-text or notebook editor components can be embedded in a Windows desktop app, and under what licenses?
Which existing libraries or OS APIs provide a draggable, always-on-top floating window on Windows 10 and 11?
Compare WinUI 3, WPF, Electron and Tauri for a notes app that needs a tiny always-on-top widget window plus a main notebook window: memory footprint, startup time and multi-window support.

What approaches keep a second window and the main notebook view in sync live on one machine (shared local database with change notifications, file watching, in-process events), and what are their failure modes?
How do OneNote, Microsoft Sticky Notes and similar quick-capture apps let users capture a note from anywhere and later find it in the notebook?
What published user research or reviews show which quick-note features users treat as must-have (instant capture, auto-save, hotkey) versus nice-to-have (formatting, colors, tags)?

done_when: Every MUST question has a SUPPORTED or CONFLICTED claim with a quoted https source, or an explicit unanswered entry naming why.
